items.q: Of the four 'most common' branches, which two both name the proximal renal artery as the site?
items.exp: Site lines: atherosclerosis — proximal renal artery (1–2 cm); Takayasu — proximal renal artery; fibromuscular dysplasia — mid to distal; polyarteritis nodosa — entire length. (Book p750)

items.q: Fill up: The page puts the word ______ in brackets after fibromuscular dysplasia, classifying it as a disease of the arterial wall.
items.exp: The young-population branch reads 'Fibromuscular dysplasia (Arteriopathy) — mid to distal renal artery'. (Book p750)

items.q: In the affected-kidney chain, the arrows carrying a '(+)' mark are the ones running into the renin–angiotensin system box and into the aldosterone box.
opts: True — both '(+)' arrows denote stimulation of the next step
False — only the arrow into the renin–angiotensin system is marked
False — the '(+)' marks appear on the normal-kidney side
True — and a third '(+)' marks the arrow into profound vasoconstriction
items.exp: The printed chain is ↓RBF/perfusion →(+) renin angiotensin system →(+) ↑aldosterone → ↑angiotensin II (↑↑) → profound vasoconstriction → ↑BP → HTN/HTN crisis. (Book p750)

items.q: A 26-year-old Indian woman with weak upper-limb pulses and severe hypertension is found to have a renal artery bruit. Which branch of the 'most common' tree fits her?
opts: Takayasu arteritis — proximal renal artery, F:m 9:1
Fibromuscular dysplasia — mid to distal artery
Polyarteritis nodosa — entire length with microaneurysms
items.exp: The Indian/Asian population branch is Takayasu arteritis with the F:m ratio printed as 9:1 and the proximal renal artery affected; FMD belongs to the general young population and PAN to young males. (Book p750)

items.q: Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis becomes symptomatic once occlusion passes:
items.exp: The overall branch reads 'Symptomatic: >80% occlusion' of the proximal 1–2 cm of the renal artery. (Book p750)
